farmers-carry.description: A loaded carry that challenges grip, posture, and whole-body stability while walking.
instructions: Stand between two dumbbells, hinge to grasp them, then stand tall with the weights at your sides.
Walk with deliberate, even steps while keeping your ribs stacked over your pelvis and the weights quiet.
Stop under control, hinge at the hips, and place both dumbbells on the floor without dropping them.
Keep your shoulders level, avoid leaning or rushing, and use a clear path with secure footing.

burpee.description: A floor-to-standing bodyweight movement combining a squat, plank, and vertical jump.
instructions: Stand with feet about hip-width apart, then squat and place both hands firmly on the floor.
Step or jump your feet back to a strong plank, then bring them forward beneath your hips.
Rise from the squat, jump vertically with hands overhead, and land softly before the next repetition.
Keep your trunk braced in the plank and land with knees tracking in line with your toes.

bear-crawl.description: A quadruped crawl that coordinates opposite limbs while the trunk stays stable.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders, knees under hips, and knees hovering above the floor.
Move one hand and the opposite foot together, alternating sides with short, quiet steps.
Pause in the hovering start position before lowering both knees gently to finish.
Keep hips low and level, press the floor away, and avoid letting your hands and feet cross.

dumbbell-thruster.description: A dumbbell front squat flowing directly into an overhead press.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height with feet in a stable squat stance and elbows slightly forward.
Squat between your hips, then drive through your feet and use the rising momentum to press overhead.
Finish tall with both dumbbells stacked over your shoulders, then lower them to the rack position before squatting again.
Keep knees aligned with toes and avoid pressing early or arching your lower back overhead.

barbell-thruster.description: A barbell front squat linked to a powerful standing overhead press.
instructions: Set the bar across the front of your shoulders with hands just outside shoulder width and elbows lifted.
Descend into a front squat, then stand forcefully and transfer that drive into a smooth overhead press.
Reach a balanced overhead position, lower the bar to your shoulders under control, and reset your brace.
Maintain an upright torso, track knees over toes, and keep the bar close as it passes your face.

dumbbell-clean-and-press.description: A dumbbell lift from a hip hinge to the shoulders, followed by an overhead press.
instructions: Stand over two dumbbells with feet about hip-width apart, hinge down, and grip them with a flat, braced torso.
Extend hips and knees, guide the dumbbells close to your body, and turn the elbows under to catch at the shoulders.
Stand fully, press both dumbbells overhead, then lower to the shoulders and hinge them back to the floor.
Keep the weights close, catch with stable knees, and avoid curling the dumbbells or overextending overhead.

kettlebell-clean-and-press.description: A kettlebell clean into the rack position followed by a controlled overhead press.
instructions: Place the kettlebell between your feet, hinge to grip it with one hand, and brace your trunk with shoulders square.
Drive the hips forward, keep the bell close, and guide your hand around it so it settles softly in the rack.
Press the bell overhead to a stacked arm, lower it to the rack, then guide it into a backswing or to the floor.
Keep your wrist straight, prevent the bell from striking your forearm, and avoid leaning away during the press.

kettlebell-swing.description: A hip-driven kettlebell movement that cycles between a backswing and a standing float.
instructions: Set the kettlebell just ahead of your feet, hinge to grip it, and tip it toward you with your back long.
Hike the bell between your thighs, then snap the hips forward so the bell floats from the hip drive.
Let the bell fall naturally into the next hinge, or guide it forward and park it softly to finish.
Keep arms relaxed, knees softly bent, and avoid squatting the swing or lifting the bell with your shoulders.

turkish-get-up.description: A staged rise from the floor to standing while keeping a kettlebell stable overhead.
instructions: Lie on your side with the kettlebell at your chest, grip it with both hands, roll to your back, press it above one shoulder, and bend the same-side knee.
Roll to the opposite elbow and hand, lift your hips, sweep the straight leg under, and settle into a half-kneeling position.
Stand with the bell overhead, reverse each stage to your back, guide the bell to your chest with both hands, then roll toward it and set it down.
Watch the bell during floor transitions, keep the loaded arm stacked, and pause whenever your balance shifts.

half-turkish-get-up.description: The opening stages of a Turkish get-up, finishing in a tall hip-supported position.
instructions: Lie on your side with the kettlebell at your chest, grip it with both hands, roll to your back, press it above one shoulder, and bend the same-side knee.
Drive through the planted foot, roll onto the opposite elbow, post on the hand, and lift your hips while keeping the bell stacked.
Lower your hips, return to the elbow, roll onto your back, guide the bell to your chest with both hands, then roll toward it and set it down.
Keep your eyes on the kettlebell, your supporting shoulder active, and each transition slow enough to stay balanced.

kettlebell-figure-eight.description: A low kettlebell pass woven around the legs in a continuous figure-eight path.
instructions: Take a wide stance, hinge with knees bent, and hold the kettlebell in one hand between your legs.
Pass the bell behind one leg to the opposite hand, bring it across the front, and weave it behind the other leg.
Complete the final pass, bring the bell to center with both hands, and stand before setting it down.
Keep your spine long, hips back, and fingers clear by making every handoff deliberate and close to the legs.

landmine-thruster.description: An angled barbell squat-to-press performed from a close two-handed hold.
instructions: Face the landmine, cup the bar end at your upper chest, and set your feet in a comfortable squat stance.
Sit into a squat, then drive up and forward to press the bar along its angled path.
Finish tall with arms extended, then guide the bar back to your chest before beginning the next squat.
Keep your heels grounded, knees aligned with toes, and torso braced rather than chasing the bar forward.

renegade-row.description: An alternating dumbbell row performed from a plank with a strong anti-rotation demand.
instructions: Grip two stable dumbbells in a high plank, place feet wider than hip-width, and form a straight line from head to heels.
Press one dumbbell into the floor while rowing the other toward your ribs without turning your chest.
Lower the dumbbell softly, regain a square plank, and alternate sides before ending with both weights grounded.
Keep hips level, elbows tracking near the body, and use dumbbells that will not roll beneath your hands.

dumbbell-devil-press.description: A burpee over dumbbells that transitions through a swing into an overhead finish.
instructions: Set two dumbbells on the floor, grip them with wrists under shoulders, and step or jump into a strong plank.
Lower your chest between the dumbbells, return to plank, bring your feet forward, and swing the weights from a hip hinge.
Extend hips and knees to guide both dumbbells overhead, then lower them under control and place them for the next repetition.
Use stable dumbbells, keep them close during the swing, and avoid rounding your back or pressing from an unstable stance.

man-maker.description: A dumbbell complex combining a push-up, alternating rows, clean, squat, and overhead press.
instructions: Start gripping two stable dumbbells in a high plank with feet set wide enough to resist rotation.
Perform a push-up, row each dumbbell once, then bring your feet forward and clean the weights to your shoulders.
Complete a front squat into an overhead press, lower the dumbbells to your shoulders, and return them to the floor.
Keep hips square during rows, maintain control through every transition, and do not let the dumbbells roll.

battle-rope-alternating-waves.description: Alternating arm waves on battle ropes maintained from an athletic stance.
instructions: Face the anchor with one rope end in each hand, soften your knees, hinge slightly, and take out excess slack.
Raise one hand as the other lowers, alternating smoothly to send continuous waves toward the anchor.
Gradually reduce the wave size, return both hands beside your thighs, and let the ropes settle.
Keep your trunk steady, shoulders down, and elbows softly bent instead of rocking your whole body.

battle-rope-double-waves.description: Synchronized battle-rope waves produced with both arms from a braced stance.
instructions: Stand facing the anchor with a rope end in each hand, knees bent, hips back, and enough tension to control the ropes.
Lift and lower both hands together in a steady rhythm, creating matching waves along the ropes.
Make the waves progressively smaller, lower both hands, and allow the ropes to stop moving before stepping away.
Hold your torso stable, keep shoulders away from your ears, and avoid locking your knees or elbows.

battle-rope-slams.description: A coordinated overhead rope lift followed by a forceful two-arm slam.
instructions: Face the anchor holding both rope ends, set your feet securely, and lower into a shallow athletic stance.
Extend through the hips and knees as both arms rise, then hinge and pull the ropes down together toward the floor.
Absorb the finish with bent knees, regain your stance, and let the ropes settle after the final slam.
Brace before each pull, keep the hinge controlled, and maintain clear space around the moving ropes.

medicine-ball-slam.description: A medicine-ball lift overhead followed by a whole-body slam to the floor.
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, hold the medicine ball at chest height, and brace your trunk.
Reach the ball overhead as you extend tall, then hinge and bend your knees while driving it into the floor.
Let the ball settle or rebound safely, squat to collect it with both hands, and stand to reset.
Use a ball intended for slams, keep your face clear of its rebound, and avoid rounding as you retrieve it.

medicine-ball-overhead-throw.description: A two-handed overhead medicine-ball throw driven by coordinated leg, trunk, and arm extension.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy target with the medicine ball in both hands and enough clear space for its return.
Dip through the hips and knees, bring the ball overhead, then extend through your legs and arms to throw it forward.
Finish balanced with arms following through, then wait for the ball to settle before retrieving it.
Confirm the target and ball suit throwing, keep the area clear, and never chase an unpredictable rebound.

sled-push.description: A forward sled drive using coordinated leg action and a rigid upper-body connection.
instructions: Grip the sled posts, lean forward from ankles to head, and stagger your feet with arms firmly extended.
Drive the floor back with short, steady steps while keeping constant pressure through both hands.
Slow your steps under control, bring the sled to a complete stop, and stand upright before releasing it.
Keep your spine neutral, knees tracking with toes, and the path clear throughout the push.

sled-pull.description: A controlled sled drag that links a firm grip and braced torso with steady backward steps.
instructions: Face the sled, hold its straps or handles securely, step back until they are taut, and bend your knees slightly.
Walk backward with deliberate alternating steps, keeping your chest tall and tension continuous through the straps.
Shorten your steps to stop the sled smoothly, then release tension only after it is fully still.
Keep hips level, track each knee over its foot, and check the path behind you before and during the pull.
